item.title: Texas appeals court overturns order barring granddaughter from family trust property
item.description: A Texas appeals court has dissolved an order barring a granddaughter from coming within 500 feet of family trust property. The court found that the lower court had failed to set a trial date and specify the required security amount. However, the wider dispute over control of the Barbara Tolbert Revocable Trust and the family's inheritance claims remains unresolved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Swiss surgeon reclaims Guinness record with 3,200 heart-shaped objects after losing it in 2024
item.description: Diana Reser, a renowned Swiss heart surgeon, proudly holds the record for the largest collection of heart-shaped artifacts, now boasting 3,200 pieces. Her passion began during her medical studies, spurred by thoughtful gifts from loved ones. Reser's eclectic assortment features both decorative items and functional accessories, while she actively champions heart health awareness. Currently, she's on the lookout for a unique heart-shaped shower head to enhance her collection.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Stable Oxoboranes Isolated: Würzburg PhD pair trap rare bond; accident unlocks new chemistry
item.description: Two doctoral students at the University of Würzburg discovered stable oxoboranes, which contain a triple bond between boron and oxygen. Their findings emerged while studying reactions with diboracumulene and ketones, producing unexpected yellow and orange solids. The three new compounds can be isolated as crystalline solids and remain stable at room temperature. This breakthrough may allow greater exploration of their properties and reactions beyond previous limitations.

item.title: Marco Rubio spent over $1.2m in taxpayer-funded flights to attend son's college games
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is facing scrutiny over his frequent trips to Florida to watch his son play college football, with a Washington Post investigation estimating that 23 military aircraft journeys cost taxpayers more than $1.2 million. While Rubio is required to use government aircraft for security reasons, the frequency of his personal trips has raised questions about taxpayer spending and official accountability.
item.dc:creator: Soror Shaiza

item.title: Australian activists ordered to destroy abattoir footage despite retaining copyright
item.description: Australia’s High Court has concluded that Farm Transparency International maintains copyright over clandestinely acquired footage, underscoring the ramifications of trespassing despite its public interest nature. Activists are compelled to dispose of the recordings, although third parties may share them legally. This landmark judgment will influence future activism and the interplay of copyright law, prompting legal experts to scrutinize the ramifications for the rights of undercover filming.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Australia's High Court overturns $1.346 million abuse compensation award, orders new tria
item.description: Australia’s High Court has ordered a retrial in the case concerning the estate of a convicted sexual abuser. The retrial is necessary after the first trial did not adequately address key pieces of evidence. The court clarified important legal principles related to unrepresented litigants and trial procedures. MTH, the survivor, is once again pursuing damages for the abuse she suffered while in foster care.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Three school colleagues receive awards for saving cyclist in cardiac arrest
item.description: Kip Knowles collapsed in cardiac arrest while cycling alone, and three school staff members intervened promptly. PE teacher Stacey Charman, cookery teacher Chellie Messenger, and school nurse Claire Agnew performed CPR for 25 minutes. Their actions, which included using a defibrillator, revived Kip before medical help arrived. Kip’s wife nominated the trio for awards from St John Ambulance for their lifesaving efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Florida chimpanzee sanctuary cut off by flooding; uses drone to deliver food to a stranded chimp
item.description: A chimpanzee named Kaleb faced isolation during heavy flooding at Save the Chimps sanctuary. Staff utilized a drone to deliver essential food and blankets to him safely. The floodwaters disrupted normal delivery routes, which required creative solutions to ensure animal welfare. By using trucks and a drone, caregivers managed to keep the animals fed and healthy, despite the challenges.

item.title: Tennessee county to pay $1 million to veteran Tasered by deputy in 2022
item.description: Knox County, Tennessee, has agreed to pay $1 million to Brian Eugene Hux, a 64-year-old disabled Air Force veteran who suffered a fractured skull and brain bleed after being Tasered by a deputy in 2022. The settlement follows a federal appeals court ruling that denied the deputy qualified immunity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mark Wahlberg's charity marks 25 years, distributing nearly $20m to help disadvantaged children
item.description: In 2001, Mark Wahlberg and Jim Wahlberg established the Mark Wahlberg Youth Foundation with a mission to uplift disadvantaged youth. Since its inception, the foundation has raised nearly $20 million, funding essential initiatives like summer camps, educational resources, and community recreation spaces. By partnering with various organizations, they strive to enhance the quality of life for children, focusing on health awareness and providing crucial support for families in need.

item.title: Mississippi homeowner's $1,385-page insurance claim rejected after 2023 fire caused $440K in damage
item.description: A Mississippi homeowner faced disappointment when her appeal for full insurance coverage following a 2023 fire was denied by a federal appeals court. Despite presenting 1,385 pages of evidence to contest her insurer's damage estimate of $440,092, the Fifth Circuit upheld the previous court's decision, highlighting the obstacles homeowners encounter in insurance disputes and concluding her quest for a fairer compensation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas businessman loses home ownership battle despite presenting evidence of a $287K bank transfer
item.description: A legal battle came to an end for a Texas entrepreneur who aimed to claim ownership of a property. The appellate court upheld the original ruling, stating that the evidence presented was inadequate to support a resulting trust. The testimony regarding a large bank transaction fell short of validating ownership, and the strict probate regulations limited the ability to appeal. Consequently, Karrie Peterson's estate retains the property.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Russian imperial family's 197-carat sapphire sells for $4.9 million, beating estimate
item.description: In Geneva, a remarkable 197.80-carat gemstone, the Romanov Sapphire from the Russian Crown Jewels, fetched an impressive $4.9 million. This piece of history, once worn by Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna, encapsulates the grandeur of imperial Russia. Following its anonymous sale by the Soviets, the gem's fascinating story has garnered the attention of collectors, underscoring the rising demand for items rich in historical significance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
